subject: Renewal discussion: premium SLA add-on & capacity top-up
body:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@oriondw.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: premium SLA add-on & capacity top-up

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for a productive quarter. As your usage has increased we wanted to put forward a concise renewal option that combines a term extension with an upgrade to our Premium SLA and a modest capacity top-up so Orion DataWorks can preserve tail-latency guarantees during your daily peak windows.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Term: 12 -> 24 months (preferred pricing applied for the longer term)
- Premium SLA: 99.9% uptime, P95 latency objective of <= 180ms, P99 guidance and incident credits for breaches
- Support: 24x7 priority response, named escalation on-call, faster incident SLAs (15m ack for Sev1)
- Capacity: +30% reserved throughput (dedicated GPU pool, isolated customer pool) with burstable capacity for unexpected traffic spikes
- Commercials: detailed in attached MAP (see MAP_Orion_2026_v2.xlsx). We kept the renewal uplift conservative to reflect the committed term.

Attachments: MAP_Orion_2026_v2.xlsx, SLA_Addendum_2026_v2.pdf (draft SLA language and addendum).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick alignment call this week to run through the MAP and SLA addendum (30 minutes).
2) If technical questions remain, loop in Karthik and Monica for a brief systems review and to schedule a perf verification run.
3) If acceptable, we can produce a PO-ready order form and DocuSign package.

Would Friday or Monday work for a short call? Happy to align to your schedule.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0129

---

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@oriondw.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@oriondw.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: premium SLA add-on & capacity top-up

Thanks Soojin —

Appreciate the concise proposal. A few clarifying questions from my side before we bring procurement in:
1) Can you confirm the exact latency SLO language you plan to put in the addendum? P95 <= 180ms is straightforward — what does the P99 guidance look like contractually?
2) How will data residency be handled for our EU customers routed through our platform? We need an assurance that data at rest for those tenants remains in eu-1 region pools.
3) For the perf verification run you mentioned — can you scope it (duration, sample traffic profile, SLO pass criteria)?

If the answers are good we can proceed to procurement. Preferred timeline: PO in by Sep 25 if we can lock terms this week.

Best —
Daniel
CTO, Orion DataWorks

---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@oriondw.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: premium SLA add-on & capacity top-up

Internal notes / quick answers for Daniel — copying him for transparency.

Karthik / Monica — can you confirm the following so I can respond to Daniel?
- Contractual SLOs: we should propose P95 <= 180ms (contractual at the premium tier) + a P99 "operational target" with credits if we miss P95. For P99, we propose an operational target of <= 400ms (not credit-bearing unless systemic). Legal typically accepts that split: contractual for P95 and operational guidance for P99.
- Data residency: Orion needs EU-residency for specific tenant traffic — Monica, can we commit eu-1 dedicated subpools and note this in the addendum? Any caveats?
- Perf run scope: proposed 24-hour ramp with a synthetic traffic profile matching Orion's peak QPS pattern (attach playback); pass criteria: P95 under 180ms for 95% of windows and no more than 1 sustained incident.

Ben — please confirm commercial impact if we give the requested +30% reserved throughput and list any accelerated setup charges.

I will draft a short email back to Daniel with these bullets and attach a revised addendum.

Thanks —
Soojin

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@oriondw.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: premium SLA add-on & capacity top-up

Hey team —

Quick technical reply for the thread:
- P95 contractual <= 180ms is achievable on a dedicated GPU pool with intelligent KV/prefix caching and continuous batching tuned to Orion's median sequence lengths.
- P99 operational guidance: 350-450ms depending on tail distribution during very large concurrent requests; we can document an operational target of 400ms.
- Data residency: we can reserve an eu-1 customer pool for EU tenant traffic; that requires a small capacity carve (isolated pool) and a short setup (2-3 business days) to validate routing rules.
- Perf verification: we can run a 24-hour verification (recommended) and a shorter 3-hour smoke run prior to PO. We'll generate a latency_benchmark_summary.csv after the verification and include request-level percentiles.

Notes on risk: if Orion expects sub-100ms P95 for heavy multimodal workloads we should not promise that in writing without dedicated smaller-sequence paths / quantization changes. Current scope is safe for text-heavy request profiles.

Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

---

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@oriondw.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: premium SLA add-on & capacity top-up

Daniel —

Thanks for the quick questions. Per the notes below we updated the addendum and MAP. Summary of the revisions: 
- SLA language: P95 contractual objective <= 180ms with a credit mechanism if P95 misses exceed the monthly threshold. P99 is listed as an operational target (<= 400ms) and will be included in monthly telemetry reports.
- Data residency: we will reserve an eu-1 pool for your EU tenant traffic; documented in section 3.2 of the addendum. Setup time: 2-3 business days after PO.
- Perf verification: 24-hour run recommended; smoke test prior to PO. Acceptance criteria documented in Appendix A of the addendum.
- Commercials: attached MAP reflects +30% reserved capacity pricing. We reduced the renewal discount slightly to keep unit economics sustainable — details in the MAP file.

Attachments: SLA_Addendum_2026_v2.pdf (tracked changes), MAP_Orion_2026_v2.xlsx, latency_benchmark_summary.csv (sample from a previous similar run).

If this aligns, next step is to provide you a PO-ready order form and I can open the DocuSign envelope. If procurement needs a separate SOW for the data residency carve we can produce one; usually the addendum suffices.

Suggested times for an internal kickoff/onboarding call next week: Tue 9/21 10:00am PT or Wed 9/22 2:00pm PT. Which do you prefer?

Best —
Soojin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@oriondw.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@oriondw.com
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: premium SLA add-on & capacity top-up

Hi Soojin —

Everything looks good from our side. We accept the 24-month term, the Premium SLA language as updated, and the +30% reserved capacity carve. Procurement will issue a PO by next Tuesday (Sep 22). Please go ahead and send the DocuSign package and schedule the kickoff for Tue 9/21 10:00am PT; the engineering and infra leads will join from Orion.

One item: please include the eu-1 routing note explicitly in the order form so procurement has a line item to reference.

Thanks for the quick turnaround — excited to keep scaling with Redwood.

Daniel
CTO, Orion DataWorks
